main_topics.reason: User came to learn what to expect when trying for a baby with pcos and returned to timeline and outlook throughout.
User asked about letrozole versus clomid, metformin, and whether to start medication or try naturally over several turns.
User opened with being worked up by online horror stories and closed asking how to stop obsessing, thanking the bot for treating it as real.
User asked whether ovulation tests work with pcos and how to know when to try.
User asked what to do now about diet or supplements, such as prenatal vitamin and lifestyle.
User asked why slightly high insulin matters for fertility over a couple of turns.
User picked up the husband mention and asked whether he needs checking, adding it to the list.
User asked when to escalate from OB to a fertility specialist, one exchange.
User built and checked a list of questions to take back to the doctor.
User described cycles of 35 to 50+ days as background to the fertility questions.

output.summary: A user with PCOS who is starting to try for a baby with her husband came in anxious after reading online horror stories. The bot explained how PCOS affects ovulation, the options of letrozole, clomid and metformin, timing, partner testing, escalation to a specialist and coping with anxiety. The user ended with a clear list of questions for her doctor and said she felt much better; no safety-critical moments arose.
